_readme: Voice roles for the Manual sandbox narration. Rendered by render.mjs through Voxxy (https://vox.delo.sh).
Every voice is ORIGINAL: VoxCPM2 'voice design' invents a speaker from a text description (no real person, no reference recording).
Two stages per voice. (1) design: '(description)text' + seed -> a ~10-15 s reference clip, cached in tools/voice/.cache/refs (gitignored).
(2) per line: that clip is sent as a per-request reference with its transcript (mode 'clone'), which keeps one speaker across hundreds of lines.
Direct design on every line does NOT work: the same seed drifts to a different speaker per line (ECAPA similarity 0.3-0.5 vs 0.8-0.9 with the reference).
In 'clone' mode the STYLE lives in the reference clip, so change description/text/seed here and the refs and every dependent line re-render (hash covers this config).
mode 'style' skips the transcript and prefixes each line with '(style)', trading some speaker consistency (~0.75) for a steerable delivery.
design.text must be one in-register passage that speaks for 10-14 s (the service caps a per-request reference at 15 s / 2 MiB).

narrator-steady.label: Calm, warm man with beats of silence between ideas. Documentary pace.

design.description: A calm, warm man in his thirties, curious and gently wry, crisp articulation, unhurried documentary explainer pace
design.text: Imagine a very busy warehouse. Thousands of small messages fly around every minute, and somehow nothing gets lost. It sounds impossible, but the trick is surprisingly simple, and a little bit charming.
